OmniRoute executor API shape (critical): ExecuteInput uses `credentials.apiKey` (no `req`/`connection`). BaseExecutor constructor is `super(providerId, { id, baseUrl })`. buildErrorBody signature is (statusCode, message, upstreamDetails?, classification?). mergeUpstreamExtraHeaders(headers, extra) mutates in place (returns void). Use mergeAbortSignals for timeouts. Return Response directly.

GitHub PR workflow: a personal repo that is a standalone mirror (parent: null) cannot be the head for `gh pr create --repo upstream`. Must `gh repo fork upstream` to get a real fork (here MeRezaRezaei/OmniRoute-1), add it as remote, push branch, then open PR.

Base-red handling: if target base branch is red (upstream issue #9985 for release/v3.8.50), add '⚠️ base-red inherited: #<issue>' to PR body and do NOT try to fix base-red failures inside the feature branch.

Private branch hygiene: to submit a provider upstream while keeping .brain/ private, cherry-pick ONLY provider source+test files into an isolated worktree under .claude/worktrees/, never include .brain/. Verified executor + test must pass before opening PR.

Web-provider in-app login ONLY for a fixed set (TOKEN_EXTRACTION_CONFIGS in open-sse/services/tokenExtractionConfig.ts, consumed by src/app/api/providers/[id]/login/route.ts + open-sse/services/inAppLoginService.ts via Playwright). Configs exist for: claude-web, chatgpt-web, gemini-web, grok-web, perplexity-web, deepseek-web, qwen-web (NOT kimi-web, NOT hy3). No config -> no browser tab opens; route returns 'No extraction config found'.

Web providers deepseek-web & kimi-web are authType:'apikey', authHeader:'bearer' => supply a SESSION COOKIE in the API Key field, NOT a username/password. Reliable method for ALL web providers: log into the site in your own browser, copy the session cookie (DeepSeek=user-token; Kimi=its auth cookie), paste into the provider connection API Key field, save, test. This bypasses the flaky Playwright in-app login entirely.

hy3 is NOT a registered provider anywhere in OmniRoute (grep 'hy3' in providers index/constants/registry = 0 hits, no registry dir). Cannot be added as-is. User likely meant a different free web provider (hunyuan/yuanbao/hailuo/qwen). qwen-web IS registered + has in-app login. kimi-web IS registered (manual cookie needed).

CDP-loopback web-login is NOT universally reliable. Reasons: (1) not all local OmniRoute installs have a Chrome to point cdpEndpoint at; (2) when the backend runs INSIDE another server (remote VPS, Docker, behind a proxy), the backend CANNOT reach the user's local Chrome loopback port (127.0.0.1:9222) because they are on different machines. Therefore the 'most reliable' driver-free login must be DASHBOARD-side: the user logs into the provider in THEIR OWN browser, and the session cookie is submitted to OmniRoute (manual paste, or a dashboard-embedded login iframe that captures the cookie client-side). A backend-controlled browser (Playwright-launch OR CDP-to-local-Chrome) only works when backend + Chrome are co-located on the same host. The earlier loopback/CDP question was about the co-located case only and does NOT solve the remote-backend case.

PENDING: when the OmniRoute backend runs inside another server (not a direct local install), confirm where the web-provider login browser interaction happens — user-side (dashboard browser) vs server-side (InAppLoginService Playwright on the backend host). If the current in-app login is server-side Playwright, a remote backend would launch a headless browser on the SERVER and could not show the user a login UI nor reach the user's local Chrome. Need to read src/app/api/providers/[id]/login/route.ts + the dashboard login component to determine the real flow for the remote case.
